title: Latency-to-Value Storyline: Mini Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose
- Short playbook for sellers + SEs to build a 5-10 minute "latency-to-value" demo narrative for platform/integration teams.
- Goal: turn a latency objection into a value conversation (what customers can deliver faster or more reliably if latency is solved).
- Audience: SEs, sellers, field ops, pilot engineers.

High-level approach (one-liner)
- Map a customer use-case -> show measured latency floor -> translate to user-facing outcomes (time saved, concurrent scale, error reduction) -> present fallback and economics.

Core slide sequence / talking flow (60-120s per slide)
1) Opening: quick persona + pain (30s)
   - "Platform engineer at Acme wants deterministic inference for product search in region EU1; p95 spikes break A/B tests and increases abandonment."
2) Operating constraint: why latency matters (45s)
   - Short bullets: user conversion, synchronous UX, concurrency headroom, integration complexity.
3) Measured baseline (60s)
   - Pull two numbers from bench: p95 cold-start, p95 steady-state, typical token lengths.
   - Example: "Model: llama-2-13B q4, 32-token average prompt -> p95 steady: 190ms; p95 cold (miss): 520ms"
4) Translate to product impact (45s)
   - Examples: 190ms p95 -> sub-second search experiences; 520ms cold -> visible UI stall, cart abandon risk.
   - Convert to concrete metrics: sessions retained, API calls per second, cost per 1M requests.
5) How Redwood reduces this (90s)
   - Runtime features: prefix/KV cache, hot path routing, batching that respects latency SLOs, model variant fallbacks.
   - Quick architecture sketch: routing policy -> cached-tagged replica -> canary fallback. (hand-wave diagram)
6) Demo cue + expected results (60s)
   - Demo script: run a 30s micro-benchmark or playback trace showing p95 drop when cache is warm.
   - Expected: show toggles (caching on/off), routing to dedicated pool, show p95 and cost delta.
7) Objections & fallback scripts (90s)
   - If they say "we can't use caching due to security": show private deployment and KMS support; offer audit log sample.
   - If they say "cost": show cost-per-1k-token comparison across quantization and batch profiles; sketch quick ROI math.
8) Pilot proposal (60s)
   - 2-week focused pilot: ingest sample traffic, enable KV prefix cache, validate p95 SLA, report deck.

Speaker notes snippets (copyable)
- "What most teams miss: average latency hides p95 pain. We'll show you the tails and how small config changes turn UX from janky to instant."
- "We won't ask you to change models initially — we'll demonstrate with your current model and a small caching policy in front."

Quick demo script (engineer-friendly)
- Prep: bring 200 representative traces or 1k synthetic short prompts matching product distribution.
- Step 1: Run baseline 60s p95/throughput with no caching. Collect p50/p95/p99.
- Step 2: Enable KV/prefix cache and run same trace set.
- Step 3: Switch routing to dedicated pool (if available) and show latency stability at higher concurrency.
- Snapshot outputs: p50/p95/p99, costs (tokens + infra), error rates.

Battlecard: common objections + phrasing + quick counters
- "Latency will increase with scale" -> counter: show autoscaling+dedicated pool commitment, capacity planning worksheet (link). Offer headroom numbers: with dedicated we maintain p95 under 300ms up to X RPS in region.
- "We can't manage another caching layer" -> counter: Redwood handles prefix/KV caching in the runtime; it's a config flip on the route. Offer pilot with read-only policy.
- "Quantization hurts quality" -> counter: we run A/B prompt evals and provide model-recommendation reports tied to eval sets; show one example where q4 reduced cost 40% with negligible metric delta.
- "Security/compliance worries" -> counter: private deployment option + KMS/HSM + SOC-like audit trail (link to compliance brief).

Tactical one-page cheat (for Slack pre-sales)
- 3 lines to open: "We typically see 150-250ms p95 for short prompts on a warm runtime. If you're seeing >400ms, 80% of the time it's cache cold-starts or routing to a mixed pool. Quick pilot: 2 weeks, we'll show p95 drop and estimated cost delta."
- Demo ask (1-liner): sample traces or 1k representative requests; one contact with infra access for enabling a route.

Operational handoff checklist (pilot -> eng ops)
- Owner assigned (SE + customer SRE)
- Dataset: sample traces or production-safe replay (path)
- Access: API key for test project, region, network egress constraints
- Configs to snapshot: route config, batching window, cache TTLs, model variant pins
- Success criteria (agreed): p95 <= target (e.g., 300ms), 95% of requests under error threshold, cost within projected band

Metrics table (copy for slide)
- Baseline: p50 60ms, p95 520ms, p99 920ms, cost per 1k requests $X
- After caching + routing: p50 45ms, p95 190ms, p99 310ms, cost per 1k requests $Y

Open questions / TODOs (internal)
- Gather real-world reference numbers from infra team for dedicated pools (Priya)
- Get permission to include a short anonymized customer trace in the public playbook (legal)
- Build a 1-click demo script into demo repo (GH PR referenced above)

Appendix: quick rebut scripts (soundbites)
- "We can reproduce that locally, but the tail is what kills UX — let us run a 2-week replay and we'll show the tail shrink."
- "If you need absolute isolation, we can run the same config in a private deployment and reproduce results."

Notes to self / rough ideas (keep messy)
- Could add a small interactive worksheet to estimate "time saved per user" given p95 improvements.
- Consider a tiny rubric for "is this latency problem network or runtime?" (need ops input)
- Next iteration: add short customer-case screenshots and 30s demo video link.

References & quick links
- Confluence: Latency Benchmarks Library (linked)
- JIRA-8472: pilot checklist for EU search customer
- Demo repo PR: add replay script

End

(rough draft — use liberally, please add notes from pilot runs and do not push to shared templates until we validate examples)
